surfaces.name: cao CLI, cao-server and Rust TUI (tmux-based orchestration)
HTTP API, in-session and ops MCP servers, AG-UI stream

claims.answer: Terminal-first: cao CLI, Rust TUI, tmux attach, plus a bundled browser Web UI served by cao-server; macOS (arm64/x86_64) and Linux x86_64 only (Windows via WSL2); no mobile app, desktop app or editor extension.

desktop_os.answer: Runs as a terminal tool on macOS (arm64/x86_64) and Linux x86_64; import-time guard rejects native Windows (WSL2 required); no packaged desktop app.

mobile_apps.answer: Bounded search finds no iOS or Android app.

browser.answer: Web UI bundled in the wheel and served at localhost:9889.

mobile_browser.answer: Phone browsers can reach the Web UI only if the server is exposed (--host 0.0.0.0) or tunnelled; no phone-specific layout or setup is documented.

cli.answer: `cao`, `cao-server`, `cao session`, `cao launch` plus a Rust `cao tui`.

editor_extensions.answer: No editor extension; MCP Apps can render in VS Code via host support but that is a host-side MCP feature.

task_actions.answer: Launch/steer via CLI, Web UI terminals and send_message; approvals happen in each provider CLI terminal (answer_user_prompt tool); review is in the terminal; resume by attaching to tmux sessions.

notifications.answer: Outbound event plugins (Discord/Slack examples) and AG-UI/MCP Apps event streams; no native push notifications.

cross_device_continuity.answer: State is in the server's SQLite and tmux; other devices can use the Web UI or SSH tunnel to the same host.

limitations: No native desktop app, mobile app or editor extension.
Windows is unsupported natively (WSL2 only).

claims.answer: Launches and controls twelve third-party coding CLIs (Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Copilot, OpenCode, Hermes, Cursor, Antigravity, OMP, Grok Build, MiniMax Code) through terminal provider adapters; models are whatever each CLI supports, with a profile `model` field; supervisor and workers can use different providers.

harnesses.answer: Twelve provider adapters in ProviderType; each runs the provider's own CLI.

model_providers.answer: Model choice is delegated to each CLI; profile `model` passes through where the provider honors it (honors_model).

custom_adapters.answer: Adapters are in-tree Python classes; no documented third-party adapter API besides a mock provider and the terminal backend contract.

session_integration.answer: Launches each provider's terminal command in tmux and drives it via PTY, status parsing and bracketed-paste input.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Profiles carry their own provider, so a supervisor and workers can run different CLIs in one session.

limitations: model_providers: Model choice is delegated to each CLI; profile `model` passes through where the provider honors it (honors_model).
custom_adapters: Adapters are in-tree Python classes; no documented third-party adapter API besides a mock provider and the terminal backend contract.

claims.answer: Each provider CLI uses its own login or API key, authenticated before launching CAO; CAO holds no credentials of its own and sells no credits.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Agents remain full CLI processes with their native authentication, so existing CLI subscription logins are used.

api_accounts.answer: API-key routes work wherever the provider CLI supports them; env vars are forwarded to panes.

local_models.answer: Possible only through provider CLIs that support local models (e.g. OpenCode); CAO has no local runtime.

account_switching.answer: Switching accounts is done inside each provider CLI; CAO does not document multi-account switching.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No CAO account needed; at least one authenticated provider CLI is required.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider terms on orchestrating their CLIs are not stated by CAO.

limitations: Subscription terms are each provider's; CAO documents the CLI guides only.
claims.unknownReason: Account switching and provider terms live in each third-party CLI and its vendor policy, not in the CAO repository.

claims.answer: Prerequisites Python 3.10+, tmux 3.3+, uv and an authenticated provider CLI; install agent profile, start cao-server, launch supervisor; works in any project directory with or without Git.

first_task_setup.answer: README First supervisor launch: cao install code_supervisor; cao-server; cao launch --agents code_supervisor.

no_git.answer: Launch runs in any directory; worktrees are optional per worker.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Git worktree isolation works on local repos; no remote needed.

hosted_git.answer: No GitHub/GitLab integration; hosted repos are clones the agents work in.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: README lists prerequisites and per-provider install/auth guides.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Remote machine access documented via SSH port forwarding; EKS reference deployment; no one-command VPS installer.

limitations: Several manual steps across two terminals; no managed-cloud setup; BYO VPS is a manual SSH/port-forward pattern.

claims.answer: Broad programmatic surface: cao CLI, HTTP API with OpenAPI and PTY WebSocket, in-session MCP server, external cao-ops-mcp server, AG-UI SSE stream, event plugins, workflow Python shim; no webhooks in; optional local-token or IdP auth.

api.answer: FastAPI routes on localhost:9889 with OpenAPI plus PTY WebSocket.

sdk.answer: Python cao_workflow authoring package and Python event-plugin API; no general SDK.

mcp_server.answer: cao-ops-mcp-server exposes launch/send/read/shutdown tools to external agents; cao-mcp-server serves in-session tools.

webhooks.answer: No inbound webhooks (event plugins are outbound).

operations.answer: Create/inspect/send/stop/read output through ops MCP, CLI and HTTP.

authentication.answer: Default off; CAO_AUTH_LOCAL_TOKEN bearer or IdP JWT with cao:read/cao:write scopes; settings.json auth keys are not wired.

stability.answer: SemVer declared in the changelog and 1.x supported; Agent Plugins and AG-UI surfaces are gated off by default.

limitations: No inbound webhooks; auth is off by default; API stability beyond SemVer 1.x not detailed.

claims.answer: Agents inherit their CLI's MCP client; CAO adds in-session MCP tools, profile-declared MCP servers, skills, event plugins and Agent Plugins 1.0.0 packages.

mcp_client.answer: Profiles declare MCP servers passed to provider CLIs; the MCP client is the provider's.

plugins.answer: Event plugins (Python entry points) and Agent Plugins via cao plugin add (gated).

custom_tools.answer: Plugins can register MCP tools through on_mcp_server; workflows add Python steps.

instructions_import.answer: Skills (SKILL.md) installed into a store and injected lazily; agent profiles carry prompts.

authentication.answer: MCP server authentication is configured per server in the profile/provider; no central secret broker beyond a secret gate for plugins.

integration_owner.answer: CAO owns in-session MCP tools; provider CLIs own their MCP client connections.

limitations: Agent Plugins surfaces are gated off by default.
MCP client behaviour is the provider CLI's.

claims.answer: Web UI is a React/Vite single-page app bundled in the Python wheel; TUI is a Rust crate; MCP App views are single-file React builds; no desktop or mobile client.

implementation_evidence.answer: web/ React source, tui/ Rust crate and cao_mcp_apps/ builds at the pinned tag.

limitations: desktop_implementation: No desktop app; browser UI and terminal clients only.

hybrids: No hybrid client.

identity_retention.answer: Terminal and session IDs persist across the run.

workflow_constraints.answer: No mandatory workflow: a supervisor can be launched directly; workflows are optional.

claims.answer: Agent profiles, skills, per-CLI instruction files, and a cross-session memory system with five scopes, search, injection and forgetting; self-learning is opt-in.

instructions.answer: Profile Markdown body becomes the agent system prompt; provider CLIs read their own instruction files.

skills.answer: SKILL.md store with lazy loading and profile scoping.

project_docs.answer: Obsidian vault / knowledge-graph docs sources documented; otherwise agents read files.

memory.answer: memory_store/recall/forget with scopes global, project, session, agent, federated.

provenance.answer: Entries are timestamped with keys and tags; per-entry source attribution limited.

correction.answer: memory_forget and CLI commands correct memories.

freshness.answer: Recency scoring and reconciliation; no explicit stale-context controls.

takeover_continuity.answer: Memory and SQLite state survive new sessions; no colleague handover feature.

evidence.title: CAO README
evidence.locator: What CAO does; Prerequisites; Install CAO; First supervisor launch
evidence.finding: Local cao-server starts provider CLIs in isolated terminal sessions and gives a supervisor tools to coordinate workers; twelve provider CLIs; install via uv from main or PyPI; Web UI at localhost:9889; Apache-2.0.

evidence.title: CAO codebase guide
evidence.locator: Runtime surfaces; Package map; Providers and terminal backends
evidence.finding: cao CLI, FastAPI cao-server, in-session cao-mcp-server, external cao-ops-mcp-server, React web UI, MCP Apps, Rust TUI; tmux/herdr backends; SQLite state; optional OpenTelemetry.

evidence.title: Control planes
evidence.locator: Surfaces at a glance; Remote fleets; cao-ops-mcp server
evidence.finding: Web UI, cao session shell CLI, cao-ops-mcp MCP tools, cao fleet/worker for remote fleets, outbound event plugins; all inbound surfaces use the HTTP API.

evidence.title: Web UI guide
evidence.locator: Starting the Web UI; Remote machine access; Features
evidence.finding: Bundled React dashboard at localhost:9889: sessions, agent spawn, profiles, flows, settings, live terminals, status badges, inbox; remote use via SSH port forwarding or --host 0.0.0.0.

evidence.title: Configuration
evidence.locator: settings.json schema; Auth (auth) env-var only; Server; Terminal backend
evidence.finding: Single settings.json with CLI>env>file>default precedence; auth is default-off with local-token or IdP JWT modes; spawn_mode and pane layouts; network and auth settings env-var only.

evidence.title: Python package manifest
evidence.finding: cli-agent-orchestrator 2.5.3, Apache-2.0, Python >=3.10; macOS and Linux classifiers only.

evidence.title: Platform guard
evidence.finding: Raises on Windows: supported macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64); Windows must use WSL2 because orchestration uses tmux.

evidence.title: Provider enumeration
evidence.finding: kiro_cli, claude_code, codex, kimi_cli, copilot_cli, opencode_cli, hermes, cursor_cli, antigravity_cli, omp, grok_cli, mcode (MiniMax Code), plus a test mock.

evidence.title: Agent profiles
evidence.finding: Profiles select provider, model, role/allowedTools, MCP servers, provider launch config (claudeConfig effort/fallback model), init timeout; install --provider overrides.

evidence.title: In-session MCP server
evidence.locator: handoff, assign, send_message, complete_assignment, list_siblings, memory_*, workflow_*, report_outcome tools
evidence.finding: Supervisor/worker tools: handoff (blocking with timeout, optional use_worktree), assign (async), send_message, complete_assignment, get_handoff_result, list_siblings, delete_terminal, memory and workflow tools.

evidence.title: Worktree service
evidence.finding: use_worktree on handoff/assign gives that worker its own git worktree and branch derived from the terminal ID; global flag and cleanup command not built.

evidence.title: Terminal status model
evidence.finding: Statuses unknown, idle, processing, completed, waiting_user_answer, error.

evidence.title: Flows
evidence.finding: Scheduled agent sessions defined as Markdown with cron schedule, agent profile and provider; cao-server must be running for schedules; manual run supported.

evidence.title: Flow service
evidence.finding: APScheduler cron trigger computes next run time inside cao-server.

evidence.title: Workflows
evidence.finding: Saved multi-step agent pipelines in Python with concurrent fan-out, durable journal and resume, step replay, optional plan approval.

evidence.title: Plan approval gate
evidence.finding: Opt-in, default-off gate refusing an unapproved script-tier workflow plan (403 when absent, 503 when store unavailable).

evidence.title: Tool restrictions
evidence.locator: Default Behavior; Three Controls; How Tool Restrictions Are Enforced
evidence.finding: role/allowedTools/--yolo controls; default developer role; enforced through provider-native flags for Claude Code, Copilot and Grok, Kiro tools; prompt-level instructions for Kimi, MiniMax and Codex.

evidence.title: Memory system
evidence.locator: Capabilities; Memory Scopes; MCP Tools; Context Injection
evidence.finding: Five scopes, markdown wiki store with SQLite index, memory_store/recall/forget MCP tools, CLI, BM25/recency search, automatic injection at session start.

evidence.title: Self-learning
evidence.finding: Opt-in, default-off outcome capture and retrospector-driven lessons promoted into profiles.

evidence.title: Skills
evidence.finding: Reusable SKILL.md folders in a global store, lazily loaded by name/description, scoped to profiles.

evidence.title: Event plugins
evidence.finding: Python event plugins in cao-server are observers for session/terminal/message events (Discord, Slack example, audit, metrics); cannot block operations.

evidence.title: Agent plugins
evidence.finding: Portable Agent Plugins 1.0.0 packages of skills and MCP servers installed with cao plugin add; surfaces gated off by default behind CAO_AGENT_PLUGINS_ENABLED.

evidence.title: OpenTelemetry deployment
evidence.finding: OTel spans and metrics are off by default (OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=false enables) and export to a collector the operator configures.

evidence.title: AG-UI event stream
evidence.finding: Default-off SSE AG-UI stream of metadata-only fleet events with replay and optional auth.

evidence.title: MCP Apps
evidence.finding: Optional host-rendered fleet UI (dashboard, agent, event stream views) inside MCP App-capable hosts such as Claude Desktop and VS Code.

evidence.title: HTTP API overview
evidence.finding: Sessions/terminals, inbox, profiles, workflows, memory, flows routes and PTY WebSocket on localhost:9889; OpenAPI served by cao-server.

evidence.title: Inbox delivery
evidence.finding: send_message queues in SQLite and delivers by bracketed paste once the target is idle, with watchdog and reconciliation sweeps.

evidence.title: Terminal lifecycle
evidence.finding: Terminals occupy tmux windows and DB records; cleanup paths snapshot state; restore documented.

evidence.title: Working directory support
evidence.finding: CAO_ENABLE_WORKING_DIRECTORY opt-in lets handoff/assign set a validated working directory.

evidence.title: Security policy
evidence.finding: GitHub advisories or AWS reporting; 48h acknowledge, 7-day assessment, 30-day target for critical issues; 1.x supported.

evidence.title: Control planes: remote fleets
evidence.finding: cao fleet/worker address a broker for agents in a cluster; EKS reference implementation under examples/cao-clusters/kubernetes/eks.

evidence.title: Fleet coordinator
evidence.finding: Example cross-node coordinator with web panel and AI conductor over multiple CAO nodes (examples/fleet).

evidence.title: Rust TUI
evidence.finding: Rust terminal UI crate (cao tui) with guided flow, handoff and results panes.

evidence.title: Changelog
evidence.finding: Unreleased section lists ephemeral agents (off by default), pane spawn mode, local-token auth, per-terminal model recording, security CI; no dated roadmap.

evidence.title: Web UI source
evidence.finding: React components: DashboardHome, AgentPanel, FlowsPanel, InboxPanel, MemoryPanel, WorkflowsPanel, ProfilesPanel, PluginsPanel, SettingsPanel, TerminalView, OutputViewer.

evidence.finding: 1563 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-11-16, homepage awslabs.github.io/cli-agent-orchestrator; latest release v2.5.3 (2026-10-08).
